title: Fermentation kinetics and biophysical characterization of ethanol production from  Citrullus colocynthis  extract
content: With the growing global demand for renewable energy and the environmental impact of fossil fuel usage, the use of sustainable lignocellulosic feedstock for second-generation (2G) bioethanol production has become an urgent need. In the present study, bioethanol production capabilities of Citrullus colocynthis fruits were explored using an integrated pretreatment, saccharification, and fermentation process, as they are a less-explored plant from the xerophytic species found in arid and semi-arid regions. The lignocellulosic composition of C. colocynthis biomass was analyzed by Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy. The obtained spectra confirmed the presence of cellulose, hemicellulose and lignin. Initially, a Central Composite Design (CCD) with Response Surface Methodology (RSM) was used with 4 independent variables, namely substrate concentration, H2SO4 concentration, incubation temperature, and incubation time, with 30 experimental runs, to optimize the dilute acid pretreatment process. All four regression models (glucose yield, xylose yield, lignin yield, and cellulose yield) were significant (p < 0.001), and the R2 values were in the range of 90.42% to 94.91%. The glucose, xylose, and cellulose models did not experience a significant lack of fit and had moderate predictive ability (predicted R2 = 59.85–68.85%), while the lignin model had a significant lack of fit (p = 0.017) and was presented as a trend only. The optimum result in terms of pretreatment was obtained for Trial 28 (4 g substrate, 3% H2SO4, 90 °C, 60 min), which was chosen because it had the highest cellulose content (65.0 ± 2.2%) and moderate lignin retention (33.1 ± 1.3%) and was used for the downstream processing. The maximum concentration of reducing sugar obtained by enzymatic saccharification of the optimally pretreated biomass with commercial cellulase (Cellic® CTec2) over 72 h was 11.27 ± 0.43 mg mL−1. The subsequent fermentation of the hydrolysate by Saccharomyces cerevisiae resulted in a maximum ethanol yield of 4.43 ± 0.11 g L−1, ethanol yield coefficient (Yp/s) of 0.44 g g−1, and fermentation efficiency of 86.1%, indicating efficient hexose utilization by S. cerevisiae. The overall results indicate that C. colocynthis fruit biomass is a promising non-food lignocellulosic feedstock for bioethanol production by laboratory scale production; further evaluation of its suitability for pilot or industrial level, including xylose utilization, process economics, etc. needs to be examined.
